hints.title: Two-Robot Simultaneous Descent Obstacle
hints.text: Two robots move down one row simultaneously from top-left and top-right corners. How can synchronizing their simultaneous row progression track the optimal column positions for both robots without double-counting shared cells?

hints.title: Row Synchronization Column Pair Invariant
hints.text: At row r, both robots are on row r at columns c1 and c2. In the next row, robot 1 can move to c1 - 1, c1, or c1 + 1, and robot 2 can move to c2 - 1, c2, or c2 + 1.

hints.title: 2D Column-Pair Table Rolling Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a table of dimensions cols x cols with -1, setting entry (0, cols - 1) to the combined cherries of both starting corners. For each row from 1 to rows - 1, compute the next row table across all 9 movement pairs (dc1, dc2 in -1, 0, 1). If both robots share a column, collect the value once, otherwise add both. Return the maximum value in the final table.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: For each row, evaluates 9 transitions for up to C^2 column pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive search explores 9^R possibilities, which is astronomical for R=70.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining only the current row column-pair table uses O(C^2) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Synchronizing row descent so robots move in lockstep through a 2D column-pair state space.
